title: Hopf bifurcations and period-doubling cascade in a two-delay predator–prey model with Holling type II response
task: Bifurcation analysis of delay differential equations in predator-prey dynamics
key_results: Period-doubling cascade with Feigenbaum ratio δ ≈ 4.6692 converging to accumulation point τ₁^∞ ≈ 18.64; alternating subcritical/supercritical Hopf bifurcations organized by Bautin bifurcations
comments: Application of classical dynamical systems theory to ecological model; the universal Feigenbaum ratio provides validation but aperiodic behavior beyond accumulation point remains unresolved.

model_io.model: Two-delay predator-prey system with Holling type II response

hypotheses.hypothesis: Combination of maturation and conversion delays generates route to chaos via period-doubling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; complete cascade from period-1 to period-32 with convergence to Feigenbaum universal ratio

hypotheses.hypothesis: Bifurcation criticality alternates with increasing maturation delay
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; organized by generalized Hopf bifurcations in parameter plane

hypotheses.hypothesis: Bistability emerges between coexistence and large-amplitude cycles
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; fold of periodic orbits produces coexistence of attractors
